newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates fall as liquidity rises more.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates fall as liquidity rises more.

text.p: Interbank rates fell further as liquidity levels continued to improve after recent volatility, dealers said.
The lower rates quoted at the 0300 GMT fixing of the Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (Klibor) by banks was another clear indication that the downtrend will continue, they said.
The inflow of funds into the market was mainly offshore money making a slow comeback, they said.
"Yes, the rates are coming back down. The offshore money is back in the market," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
The dealers said activity remained mainly concentrated on the one-month rate, with a large local bank doing most of the lending. "They are giving at 7.50 to all," said another dealer.
The one-month rate was at 8.0 percent on Wednesday.
The one-, two- and three-week money were at 7.40/50 percent from 7.50/80 on Wednesday.
Three-month money was at 7.50/60 percent from 7.50/8.0.
The ringgit-swap rates were also quoted lower, with one-month swaps at 25/30 against 30/35 previously.
Dealers said they were awaiting the release of Malaysia's first quarter gross domestic product data (GDP) and April money supply numbers which could give clues to interest rate direction.
Bank Negara was expected to release the GDP data on Friday and money supply next week.
Economists expect the GDP growth to be around 8.0-8.2 percent, against 8.3 in the first quarter of 1996. "I think there shouldn't be any surprises," said an economist in Singapore.
In the futures market, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate contracts which were higher across the board.
The spot June 1997 contract was up three basis points to 92.50, or an implied yield of 7.5 percent.
September 1997 contract was also up three 92.62, or 7.38 percent and December rose 92.65, or 7.35 percent.
